title: Cross-Science Invention Synthesizer — Overview and definition
t: Cross-Science Invention Synthesizer — Overview and definition
description: Combines discoveries from many sciences into new designs. (Proposed capability.)
body: Public edition. Public tool knowledge, fact-checked reference. Combines discoveries from many sciences into new designs. (Proposed capability.) A cross-science synthesizer would map mechanisms from biology, physics, chemistry, and computing onto engineering problems by analogy, then test the mappings. Analogical transfer is demonstrated in narrow cases; a general synthesizer is speculative. Status: speculative. Capability status: PROPOSED. This database describes a proposed capability, not a completed product. Status taxonomy used throughout: speculative (no demonstrated path), simulated (works in simulation only), experimentally-demonstrated (lab demo exists), independently-verified (reproduced by a third party). Generating a design cannot make impossible physics possible; every record states which status its claims carry. Capability status for this tool: speculative.

title: Cross-Science Invention Synthesizer — Teaching-ladder exercise
description: Combines discoveries from many sciences into new designs. (Proposed capability.)
body: Public edition. Public tool knowledge, fact-checked reference. Teaching ladder for Cross-Science Invention Synthesizer, simple to complex. Rank 1: name the tool's single core action (Cross-domain mechanism retrieval). Rank 3: run it once on a tiny input and check the output. Rank 5: combine two capabilities: Cross-domain mechanism retrieval and Analogy mapping with breakage checks. Rank 7: chain its output into a neighboring tool (Universal Invention Engine) with a verification checkpoint. Rank 9+: automate the full workflow and teach it to someone else. Capability status for this tool: speculative.
